KyoubeAI 1.18 lets Claude and other assistants work with a project's files and start app tasks.

## What's in 1.18.0

**Project files.** 8 new tools let a connected assistant list a project's folders and files, read a text file in pages of up to 2000 lines, write and edit files, create folders, and move and delete. A file's `modifiedAt` comes back with every read and listing; send it back as `expectedModifiedAt` and a write or edit is refused if the file changed since. `createOnly` refuses to replace a file, and an edit must match exactly once unless `replaceAll` is set. A file that is not text comes back as a link to open in KyoubeAI. Your company role and need-to-know visibility still decide every call. The guide is [docs/mcp.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/docs/mcp.md#project-files).

**App tasks.** 4 new tools list, check, start and cancel the tasks an app's templates define. `kyoubeai_apps_get` shows the templates, and starting one runs the same checks as the app's button, so the assistant meets the same refusals with their reasons ([docs/mcp.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/docs/mcp.md#app-tasks)).

**37 KyoubeAI tools.** That is 12 more than 1.17, and 72 on the connection with the core's own. Writing, editing, deleting and cancelling a task are marked destructive, so assistants that ask before a destructive call will ask. The connection now reaches `kyoube.apps` and `kyoube.files` by tool name and no longer remembers a failed answer, so a plugin that has just come up is seen on the next listing. `kyoube doctor` counts both and warns if `kyoube.files` is not answering.

**How it was tested.** The full smoke run passed on a fresh instance, with `kyoube doctor` reporting 37 KyoubeAI tools. On a separate fresh instance on `localhost`, the official MCP TypeScript SDK client signed in with OAuth (dynamic client registration, authorization code with PKCE, a loopback callback), with the consent approved in a headless browser as the signed-in person. It listed 72 tools, and the four destructive ones were marked as such. It then listed a project's folders, created a folder and a file, read it, edited one line using the `modifiedAt` it had read, and read that line back. It created and published an app with a task template, started the task, and checked it three times: it was waiting, then working once the agent picked it up. In the smoke run, a path out of the project folder was refused, and so was a write over a read-only connection. A signed-in check from Claude Code itself is still to do.

## Update

From 1.17, run `./update.sh`. It backs up first, and `./update.sh --rollback` returns to 1.17.0 from that backup. The core and its database are unchanged, `kyoube.apps` moves to 0.16.0 and `kyoube.files` to 0.5.0 on the next start, and there is nothing to set up. Assistants see the new tools the next time they list tools ([docs/upgrading.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/docs/upgrading.md#moving-to-118)).

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
